steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Land = all natural resources (farmland, oil, water). Reward: rent. Labour = human effort and skills. Reward: wages.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Capital = man-made resources used in production (machinery, factories). Reward: interest. Enterprise = the entrepreneur who organises and takes risk. Reward: profit.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Scarcity means resources are limited but wants are unlimited — the fundamental economic problem that forces choices.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Opportunity cost is the benefit of the next best alternative foregone when making a choice. E.g. if government spends on defence, the opportunity cost is the healthcare that could have been funded instead.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Identify the four factors of production and the reward each receives. | Explain what is meant by scarcity and why it is the fundamental economic problem. | A government has £10bn to spend on hospitals OR schools. Explain the opportunity cost of choosing hospitals.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always state the REWARD alongside each factor: land→rent, labour→wages, capital→interest, enterprise→profit. Opportunity cost must reference the NEXT BEST alternative, not all alternatives combined. Scarcity is not the same as shortage: scarcity is permanent, shortage is temporary.
